newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian court rejects Berlusconi plea over judge.
newsitem.headline: Italian court rejects Berlusconi plea over judge.

text.p: An Italian appeal court on Monday rejected a request by former prime minister Silvio Berlusconi for the removal of a judge presiding over a trial in which the media tycoon is accused of corruption, judicial sources said.

The decision means the trial, in which Berlusconi and his younger brother Paolo are accused of complicity in paying alleged bribes to tax inspectors, will continue with judge Carlo Crivelli remaining on the bench.
The sources said the appeal court's decision rejecting the request that Crivelli be dismissed on grounds of bias had been deposited at the Milan court earlier on Monday.

Berlusconi, who denies charges of complicity in payment of alleged bribes by four companies in his Fininvest business empire, alleged along with Paolo and two other defendants early in October that Crivelli was actively siding with the prosecution.

He based his suit on a private exchange between Crivelli and prosecutor Gherardo Colombo in which Crivelli spoke of a "carrot and stick". The conversation, outside formal proceedings, was picked up on court microphones and transcribed.
Berlusconi's lawyer said Crivelli's recorded remarks cast serious doubt on his impartiality.
But Crivelli told the court last month the remarks had been a reminder to Colombo that he intended to strike a balance between prosecution and defence.

Berlusconi, prime minister for seven months in 1994, is accused of having conspired in the payment of bribes of 380 million lire ($250,00) to tax police by four of his companies for lenient audits between 1989 and 1991.

The media tycoon, who leads the opposition centre-right Freedom Alliance, has denied knowledge of the payments at the time they were made, argues that they were in fact extorted from his group by the tax police, and says the case is part of a political plot to ruin him.
